settings_schema.header:
Configure OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication with Authentik for your Mattermost instance. Works on Team Edition without an Enterprise license.

Notice: This is an independent 3rd party tool developed by Christopher Turner (https://christopherturner.io), not affiliated with or endorsed by Mattermost, Inc. or Authentik.
settings_schema.footer:
Authentik Setup: In Authentik, create an OAuth2/OpenID Provider with Redirect URI: https://mattermost.company/plugins/io.christopherturner.mattermost-authentik/oauth2/callback. Attach the provider to an Application and configure the matching credentials below.

Disclaimer: Authentik for Mattermost is an independent, third-party plugin developed by Christopher Turner (https://christopherturner.io). Not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by Mattermost, Inc. or Authentik.

settings.help_text: When true, users can log in via Authentik OpenID Connect.

When enabled, automatically disables standard email/username and password login across Mattermost so all users must authenticate via Authentik SSO. Make sure you have a working Authentik admin before enabling.
Base URL of your Authentik instance (e.g. https://authentik.company).

The slug of the Authentik Application configured for Mattermost (e.g. mattermost). This automatically derives the discovery endpoint: <AuthentikURL>/application/o/<slug>/.well-known/openid-configuration.
If provided, overrides the auto-computed Authentik discovery URL. Must be an OIDC discovery endpoint or provider issuer URL.
The Client ID generated by Authentik for the OAuth2 Provider.
The Client Secret copied from the OAuth2 Provider in Authentik.
Optional. Paste the PEM-encoded root CA certificate or self-signed certificate for Authentik. Required if Authentik uses a self-signed certificate or an internal private CA.
When enabled, TLS certificate verification is disabled for all connections to Authentik. Use with caution, intended for development and test environments.
OAuth scopes to request from Authentik. Default: openid profile email
Authentik group name (e.g. 'mattermost-admins' or 'authentik Admins'). Users in this group will be granted System Administrator privileges in Mattermost.
If enabled and an Admin Group is configured, users will have their System Admin role granted or revoked based on their Authentik group membership on each login.
Team handle (URL name) that new users will automatically be added to upon first login.
When true, users who do not already have an account in Mattermost will be automatically created on first successful Authentik login.
When true, existing accounts with a matching email address will be linked to Authentik on first login.
When true, logins will be rejected if Authentik reports that the user's email address has not been verified.
Text displayed on the login button.
Background color of the login button (HEX code). Default is Authentik Orange (#FD4B2D).
Verify connectivity to Authentik, test OpenID Connect discovery, validate JWKS keys, and check Client ID / Secret.
View and manage leftover LDAP-locked accounts. You can unlock them to standard accounts (which makes them editable in System Console and allows linking to Authentik) or deactivate them.
